comments.body:
SUPERSEDED — folded into bug b636 (allpurpose-rainy-discus) and its change 1559.

Splitting the restore into a dependent story created a review-ordering deadlock: linking
9f7f depends_on b636 made review-plan fast-fail INDETERMINATE until b636 closed, so fsck
would have shipped able to DETECT a known-auto-repairable class (505 live tickets, 504 fully
recoverable) while declining to repair it. The restore now lands in b636 itself.

The two blocking plan-review findings earned here were carried into b636's plan:
(1) reuse the ticket-scoped single-pass history walk from
    attest.authorship.build_ticket_position_commit_map rather than re-deriving it; and
(2) that helper folds OLDEST-wins, correct for --diff-filter=A, but a --diff-filter=D walk
    must take the NEWEST deletion or it restores a stale pre-image for a path deleted twice.
Both are now acceptance criteria on b636 with a held-out test each.

compiled_state.description:
# fsck should RESTORE deleted sources, not just refuse

## STACKED ON UNLANDED CHANGE 1557 (bug b636) — read this first
This story is the SECOND change in a stack. Gerrit change 1557 (bug `b636`) is unlanded at
the time of writing, and it INTRODUCES the symbols this plan builds on. They do NOT exist on
`origin/main` yet:
- `compact_rebuild.snapshot_missing_sources(ticket_dir)` — the cited-but-absent-source
  predicate (1557 also extracts the whole rebuild cluster from `compact.py` into the new
  `_commands/compact_rebuild.py` leaf for the module-size cap).
- `fsck._maybe_repair_snapshot(...)` — 1557 extracts the previously INLINE repair block from
  `fsck._scan` (main's fsck.py:180-190) into this helper.
- the `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES` fsck finding.
Do not start this story until 1557 has merged; re-verify these names against the merged tree
before implementing.

## Why
1557 makes the rebuild FAIL CLOSED when the prior SNAPSHOT cites source events absent from
disk. That stops new corruption but leaves the population permanently un-repairable: a dry run
of the fixed fsck reports 505 live tickets in that shape, and `fsck --repair` can then never
drive them to fsck-zero.

## Evidence restoration is possible
Deleted event files remain reachable in `origin/tickets` history at the deleting commit's
parent. Over the 505 flagged tickets: 504 have deletion records covering every cited-missing
uuid, 1 partial, 0 with none. Validated on a COPY of the live store: restoring every deleted
event file then rebuilding restored 214/214 already-regressed tickets (486 events).

## Prior art to REUSE, and where it must DIFFER
`attest/authorship.py:build_ticket_position_commit_map` is the ticket-scoped, single-pass
`git log --diff-filter=A --name-only` walk, cost-tuned as the batched form of
`resolve_event_commit`. Reuse that SHAPE.
CRITICAL DIFFERENCE: that helper streams newest->oldest and OVERWRITES, so the OLDEST commit
wins — correct for `--diff-filter=A` (the oldest ADD introduced the event). For
`--diff-filter=D` the correct fold is the NEWEST deletion (the last time the path was
removed), because a path may be added and deleted more than once across successive
compactions. Copying the oldest-wins fold direction would read a stale pre-image. Use
first-seen-wins over the newest-first stream, and TEST a path deleted twice.
Blob reads use the existing `git show <ref>:<path>` idiom (`binding_store.py`,
`_store/compat.py`).

## Naming
`_commands/fsck_recover.py` already owns 'recover' here, so the new primitive is
`restore_deleted_sources`.

## Why the snapshot's citation list is not enough
Ticket 72d5 recovered its close STATUS but still read in_progress: an EARLIER deleted STATUS
that no surviving snapshot cites broke the chain's current_status precondition, so the reducer
rejected both it and the close. Restoration must sweep the ticket's FULL deletion history.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `compact_rebuild.restore_deleted_sources(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir) -> list[str]`
      restores every event file deleted from that ticket dir, enumerated by ONE ticket-scoped
      `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- <tid>/` pass, NEWEST-deletion-wins, each blob
      read at the deleting commit's parent and written back as a folded `.retired` source
      (never resurrected live). Returns restored filenames.
- [ ] `compact_rebuild.rebuild_with_restore(...)` owns restore -> re-check
      `snapshot_missing_sources` -> rebuild, refusing (1557 fail-closed) only when restoration
      cannot complete the log.
- [ ] BOTH live rebuild call sites route through it: `fsck._maybe_repair_snapshot` (post-1557)
      and `fsck_repair.py:268`. Neither may call `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` directly.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports per ticket how many events WOULD be restored and whether a rebuild
      would follow, writing nothing.
- [ ] Per-ticket scan only (no full-history index build) so it stays usable on a large store.
- [ ] BACK-OUT + blast-radius: the run pre-tags the tracker before any write (as A3 did, but
      the tag MUST be created before the FIRST batch — `pre-a3-remediation` was stamped
      mid-run, after 2 of 4 batches, and is therefore not a valid rollback point). Before any
      live run, the whole sweep is executed against a COPY of the store and the resulting
      status of EVERY ticket is diffed against the pre-run state; only the intended
      restorations may change status.
- [ ] Held-out test: a ticket whose close exists ONLY in history is restored and reads closed
      after `fsck --repair`.
- [ ] Held-out test: a path deleted TWICE restores the newest pre-image, not the oldest.
- [ ] Held-out test: a ticket with genuinely unrecoverable sources still refuses, unchanged
      from 1557.

held-out tests for recovery and for the still-unrecoverable refusal
